about: How a build is sized, and the documents each rule comes from. src/lib/sizing.ts applies it; the build pages show it. Every source is fetched, checked for its quotes and archived by `pnpm sizing:sources`, which stamps fetched and snapshot_hash. Edit a rule only together with its source.

kv_cache.rule: Each person's session keeps its conversation in memory (the KV cache), and that memory grows with every token. We work out the memory per token from the model's own published configuration with the formulas below, at 16-bit. Layers that keep a fixed-size state instead of a growing cache are not counted.

vllm.rule: vLLM, the inference server, uses 92% of GPU memory by default. The weights and every session must fit in that.

llama.cpp.rule: llama.cpp, the inference server, fits the model and its sessions into memory and leaves 1 GiB free on each GPU. The weights and every session must fit in what remains.

mlx.rule: MLX publishes no rule for how much memory it leaves usable, so we do not estimate a fit for MLX builds.

apple_unified_memory.rule: On a Mac, macOS lets the GPU use only part of the unified memory and does not publish how much. We show the sum against total memory and confirm the fit by measuring.

measured.rule: Once a build is running, vLLM reports at startup how many sessions of a given length its memory holds ("Maximum concurrency for N tokens per request"). We save that line with the build, and it replaces the estimate.
